assessment.evidence_level_reason: Live execution on real websites and Windows apps with observed end states (12 cases), alongside offline synthetic classification; judging protocol unstated -> minimal online evidence; transfer not adopted (SC1).
assessment.author_claim_kept: ResponsibleTA's feasibility/completeness/security capabilities make LLM task automation responsible, improving success and efficiency; DSM guards beat prompted LLMs.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: On 12 author-chosen live tasks (web sites + Windows 11/Outlook), single runs judged by an unstated criterion, the full ResponsibleTA pipeline with a GPT-4 coordinator completed 10/12 vs 3/12 for a coordinator that never sees the screen (+Fea alone 8/12); the gain mixes guard verdicts with screen information supplied on replanning. On synthetic random-split test pairs, trained pixel guards beat 1-shot GPT-4 over parsed text (feasibility Acc 74.8 vs 68.9; completeness 83.8 vs 62.9). Privacy placeholders preserved task outcome in 2 cases; no leakage was measured.
cannot_say: the feasibility/completeness verdicts (rather than screen information or retries) cause the success gain
guards are reliable on real agent steps
privacy is protected (no leakage test; screen text sent on replanning)

G.reason: Real limitation with concrete cases (planner issues commands with no matching element; execution incomplete; private literals sent to a cloud LLM; Fig. 4/6-8). But the premise that existing systems only use summary descriptions is asserted (B16), the lineage stops at SayCan-style critics and robotics/game execution-feedback planners (B17, B18), and GUI self-critique/feedback agents available before this version (RCI, arXiv 2303.17491, described in batch material X01) are neither cited nor compared, while a novelty claim is made (B19). Residual gap relative to self-correcting GUI agents is therefore unbounded -> 2 (son55), not 3 (sol).

M.reason: Pre-execution feasibility gate, post-execution completeness check, replanning on negative verdicts and placeholder substitution are concrete and target named failure points. Key assumptions weak: guard reliability on real on-policy commands is untested, completeness uses a single post-action frame and a presence-based criterion (B27, F05), and the design simultaneously adds screen information to the planner (I01). Both seats agree.

X.reason: Architectures, output tokens, datasets, training settings and full prompts are reconstructable (Fig. 2/5, App C.1). Missing: replanning cap value (B15), how the 12 tasks were chosen/run, threat model and NER recall for the security module (B14), handling of guard errors. Failure boundary shown (B25). Both seats agree.

E.measurement.reason: Guard metrics are computed on synthetic pairs whose negatives are fabricated captions/items (B03, B04), so they measure a constructed proxy rather than reliability on real infeasible or incomplete steps; the LLM paradigm is measured through a noisy parser (B22) with a 1-shot prompt (F02). The system-level outcome is a binary author mark on 12 single runs with no stated judge or criterion (B12), and 'valid steps' is undefined. Above 0 because a labelled test set and per-case progress exist; below 2 because neither measurement validly tests the central claim (verifier reliability, success improvement). 1 (son55) rather than 2 (sol).

E.causality.reason: Sequential Baseline / +Fea / +Fea+Com on the same coordinator is a start, but the Baseline never receives screen information while guard arms do on replanning (I01, B20), there is no +Com-only arm, no matched-retry or screen-info-only control, and the LLM-vs-DSM comparison differs in input modality and supervision (F02, B22). Both seats agree.

E.holdout.reason: Guard test splits are random pair-level splits of the same synthetic generator (B08), site-level separation unstated; the 12 live tasks are author-chosen with no development/test separation (B11); security tested on 2 cases (B13). Both seats agree.

E.statistics.reason: One run per task/configuration, 12 tasks, no intervals; per-case progress and both residual failures disclosed (I02, B25). Both seats agree.

E.cost.reason: Efficiency is claimed via valid/total steps only; no calls, tokens, latency or replanning counts; extra guard and parser calls per step unmeasured; training hardware given (B24). Both seats agree.

status_reason: Full text and appendices read; prompt figures 2/5 checked (1-shot, parsed-text input; baseline without screen elements confirmed from §3.1); all eight items resolved.

Besides Table 1, the paper executes 12 tasks live on real sites and Windows apps with recorded trajectories (Fig. 4, 6-8; B09, I02), whose end state is the execution result; rule 3 concerns learned verifiers, not this. The unstated judging criterion and n=12 are evidence-quality problems scored in E.measurement=1/E.statistics=1, not a reason to relabel the type. Transfer considered and not adopted (see SC1).

resolutions.reason: A narrower conclusion is determinable from the reported data (author report): the complete pipeline outperformed a screen-blind baseline on 12 single-run cases, and trained guards beat prompted GPT-4 on synthetic pairs. What cannot be said - that the verdicts themselves cause the gain, that guards are reliable on real trajectories, that privacy is protected - is recorded in cannot_say. son55's confound (I01) is adopted into the narrowed claim text; value stays scoped.
